families.summary: AISAP CARDIO V1.0 is machine-learning decision-support software (product codes POK/QIH, 21 CFR 892.2060) that processes acquired adult cardiac POCUS DICOM images and reports a 2-level (none-mild vs more than mild) and 4-class ASE-category assessment of mitral, tricuspid and aortic regurgitation and aortic stenosis, plus LVEF, LVEDD, RV FAC, IVC diameter, aortic root diameter and atrial areas. Cleared 2024-08-01 (K234141) with Ultromics EchoGo Pro (K201555) and EchoGo Core 2.0 (K213275) as predicates, supported by standalone measurement (200 cases), standalone valve (329 cases) and MRMC (260 cases) studies on prospectively collected POCUS exams from 4 US/Israel sites.
families.intended_use_quote: AISAP CARDIO V1.0 is a software platform that automatically processes and analyzes acquired cardiac POCUS images, producing a report with diagnostic assessment and measurements of several key cardiac structural and functional parameters, including: presence of valvular pathology (regurgitations of the mitral, tricuspid, aortic valves and aortic stenosis), and measurements of the Left Ventricle Ejection Fraction (LVEF), right and left ventricular dimensions, right ventricular fractional area change (RV FAC), atrial areas, ascending aorta diameter, and inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter. The device outputs are provided in a report that is intended to support qualified physicians in their analysis and interpretation of adult cardiac POCUS images, using FDA-cleared ultrasound devices. Physicians should be trained and privileged by their organization following education processes and should perform cardiac POCUS according to their specialty professional society clinical guidelines. AISAP CARDIO V1.0 has not been validated for the assessment of congenital heart disease, and/or intra-cardiac lesions (e.g., tumors, thrombi, vegetations), prosthetic valves, and in the presence of ventricular assist devices. AISAP CARDIO V1.0 is indicated for use in adult patients only.

training_data.description: 'The AISAP CARDIO V1.0 algorithms were trained at 2 academic institutions that perform cardiac ultrasound examinations and interpretations according to ASE guidelines. Over 140,000 individual exams were used for training the machine learning models representing > 1 billion frames.' (p.5). Training cohort table (p.6): age 67±16.73 y; 39.6% female; POCUS device (not high-end cardiac system) 25.9%; bedside exam outside echo lab 23.8%; cardiac valve disease of any severity 40.7%; hypertension 41.9%; IHD 17.5%; DM 15.2%; HF/CMP 5.8%. n_studies is a floor ('over 140,000').

validation_data.description: 'The study cohort consisted of cardiac POCUS exams that have been collected prospectively at 4 clinical reader sites in the United States (51% of cases) and Israel.' 260 de-identified cases for the reader study, 329 for the standalone valve study, 200 for the standalone measurement study; average 23.7 loops per case; vendors Philips 41%, GE 28%, Wisonic 12.5%, EchoNous 18.5%; 13% Black or African, 5.5% Asian, 4% Hispanic or Latino (p.8-9). Whether the three study cohorts overlap is not stated.

prior_validations.description: AISAP FDA-clearance press coverage (DAIC, Aug 2024) states MRMC clinical trials were run at six institutions (Mass General Brigham, Thomas Jefferson University Hospital, Mayo Clinic, Inova Fairfax, Crozer-Chester, Stony Brook), that the model was 'trained on hundreds of thousands of studies comprising over 24 million echo video clips', and cites '93 percent sensitivity and 93 percent specificity' for valve pathology. These figures differ from the FDA summary (4 reader sites; >140,000 exams) and are company-sourced.

Prospective single-arm study of AI-enhanced handheld FoCUS by non-cardiologists at Sheba (NCT05455541; AISAP CARDIO V0.7 per registry): 660 patients; clinically relevant findings in 193 (29%); therapy adjusted in 49 (7%).

External validation at Mayo Clinic Health System of the Aisap.ai atrioventricular regurgitation deep-learning algorithm on TTE (2013-23): predictions returned for 578/1541 studies (38%); MR AUC 0.98, TR AUC 0.96.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Cardiac Point-of-Care Ultrasound: A Prospective Single-Arm Study
papers.key_result: Prospective single-arm study (NCT05455541, Jul 2022-Dec 2023) of handheld FoCUS with AI algorithms by non-cardiologist physicians in ED/internal medicine: clinically relevant findings in 193/660 (29%), therapy adjusted in 49 (7%), interventional procedures in 9 (1.4%); high sensitivity for reduced LV function and valvular disease, lower for right-sided abnormalities.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence assessment of valvular disease and ventricular function by a single echocardiography view
papers.key_result: Single A4C-view deep-learning model trained/validated on 120,127 studies from a tertiary center; retrospective AUCs 0.883 (MR), 0.913 (TR), 0.940 (RV dysfunction), 0.982 (LVEF<=40%); prospective handheld POCUS cohort of 209 patients (NCT05455541) AUCs 0.72, 0.87, 0.95, 0.97. Relationship to the cleared V1.0 multi-view pipeline is not stated. A Correction to this article was published (Front Digit Health 2026, doi 10.3389/fdgth.2026.1815054, PMID 41878373); content of the correction not reviewed here.

papers.title: Deep learning for atrioventricular regurgitation diagnosis: an external validation study
papers.key_result: External validation of the Aisap.ai algorithm on Mayo Clinic Health System TTEs: model returned predictions for 578/1541 (38%); MR (n=280) AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), 91% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, 89% specificity; TR (n=298) AUC 0.96 (0.94-0.98), 84% accuracy, 91% sensitivity, 80% specificity.

Training set: 'over 140,000 individual exams' at 2 academic institutions; number of patients not stated. Company press coverage cites 'hundreds of thousands of studies / 24 million clips' and six MRMC institutions, which does not match the FDA summary (4 reader sites).
Sensitivity/specificity operating points for the standalone valve study are given without the threshold definition.
No peer-reviewed publication of the FDA pivotal standalone/MRMC dataset was found on PubMed in this session.
Training cohort BMI row reads 'BMI 15 to 49 (mean 6±18)' in the summary, which appears to be a typographical error in the source.

families.summary: EchoSolv AS is standalone cloud-based decision-support software (product code POK, 21 CFR 892.2060) that ingests TTE measurements plus age and body-surface area (no image analysis) and outputs a low/medium/high probability of a severe-AS phenotype (predicted AVA <=1.0 cm2) together with a 2020 ACC/AHA guideline-based severe-AS check. Cleared 2024-10-04 (K241245) with Ultromics EchoGo Pro (K201555) as predicate; the model was developed on 631,824 individuals / 1,077,145 TTEs (70:30 train/test) and validated on an independent 6,268-study retrospective cohort (AUROC 0.948) and a 5-reader, 200-case MRMC study.
families.intended_use_quote: EchoSolv AS is a standalone, cloud-based decision support software which is intended to be used by board certified cardiologist to aid in the diagnosis of Severe Aortic Stenosis. EchoSolv AS analyzes basic patient demographic data and measurements obtained from a transthoracic echo examination to provide a categorical assessment as to whether the data are suggestive of a high, medium or low probability of Severe AS. EchoSolv AS is intended for patients who 18 years or older who have an echocardiogram performed as part of routine clinical care (i.e., for the evaluation of structural heart disease).
families.indications_for_use_quote: EchoSolv AS is a machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) -based decision support software indicated for use as an adjunct to echocardiography for assessment of severe aortic stenosis (AS). When utilized by an interpreting physician, this device provides information to facilitate rendering an accurate diagnosis of AS. Patient management decisions should not be made solely on the results of the EchoSolv AS analysis. EchoSolv AS includes both the algorithm based AS phenotype analysis, and the application of recognized Aortic Stenosis clinical practice guidelines. Limitations: EchoSolv AS is not intended for patients under the age of 18 years or those who have previously undergone aortic valve replacement surgery.
embedded_ai_features: Severe AS phenotype probability (high/medium/low) from echo measurements + demographics, independent of LVOT/continuity-equation inputs
Severe AS guideline assessment (AV peak velocity, mean gradient, AVA vs 2020 ACC/AHA definition)
CSV upload for retrospective batch analysis
Third-party integration returning outputs to PACS/reporting systems

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Versus predicate (EchoGo Pro, stress-echo CAD): resting TTE measurement inputs (sonographer-entered) plus age and BSA rather than semi-automated image-derived measurements; outputs high/medium/low probability of severe AS; adds CSV upload for retrospective analysis and output integration to PACS/reporting.

performance_claims.quote: Kappa for unassisted and assisted reads were 0.641 (95%CI: 0.597 -0.685) and 0.667 (95%CI: 0.623 -0.711), respectively. When assisted with EchoSolv AS, there was an improvement in reader concordance of 0.027.

training_data.description: 'The EchoSolv AS AI Model was developed on a dataset consisting of 631,824 individuals with 1,077,145 transthoracic echocardiograms (TTE). The dataset was randomly split (ratio 70:30 based on individuals) into two separate groups, training and test set. Data from 442,276 individuals (70%) were entered into the AI model to train the device to detect severe AS cases. The remaining 189,548 individuals (30%) were reserved for internal testing. Individual patients appeared only once in either the training or test dataset but not both.' (p.6). Number of TTEs in the training partition alone is not stated. The FDA summary does not name the data source. The same 631,824-individual / 442,276-training cohort is described in Strange 2023 (Open Heart, PMID 37491129), whose abstract does not name the database; the NEDA methodology paper by the same group (Strange 2018, PMID 30098706) states NEDA data will inform AI-based aortic stenosis analyses.

validation_data.description: Standalone: 'independent retrospective cohort study. Overall, 6,268 studies were included' (p.8), US-style race categories reported; reference standard AVA<=1 cm2 verified by US board-certified cardiologists blinded to device output; a reference-standard verification analysis on an additional cohort is reported in labeling. MRMC: 200 studies (100 severe AS / 100 controls) from one US investigational site, 'to ensure the test data was independent from the training dataset' (p.9). Internal test set: 189,548 individuals held out from development data.

prior_validations.description: Proof-of-concept AI detection of severe AS on 530,871 echocardiograms (NEDA).

Mixture-density-network AI-DSA trained on 442,276 individuals (70% of 631,824; 1.08 million echos) to predict AVA<1 cm2; AUROC 0.986 (0.985-0.987) in test set; high-probability group 5-year mortality 67.9% vs 19.2% low-probability (age/sex-adjusted OR 2.41).
US external cohort: 31,141 Medicare beneficiaries at an academic medical center (2003-2017); AI-DSA sensitivity 82.2%, specificity 98.1%, c-statistic 0.986 for AVA<1 cm2 phenotype.

Retrospective two-centre cohort (9,189 adults with native aortic valves): AI alert increased guideline-defined severe AS cases from 218 to 376 (2.4% to 4.1%), with women disproportionately under-diagnosed.

Company/press: EchoSolv AS deployed at Mount Sinai Health System (Apr 2026); company claims training on '200M+ measurements' and validation against ~1 million studies; earlier press claims a trial identified 72% more severe-AS patients than human diagnosis alone. (GlobeNewswire URL could not be fetched on 2026-09-05 and MobiHealthNews returned HTTP 403; these figures are unverified. The company's own aortic-stenosis page states '200M+ Measurements', '24.1% Reduction Review Time', '82.2% Sensitivity Detection Rate', '99.2% NPV Rules Out Severe AS' and 'EchoSolv AS is cleared for use in the United States (FDA) only'.)

papers.title: Enhanced Diagnosis of Severe Aortic Stenosis Using Artificial Intelligence: A Proof-of-Concept Study of 530,871 Echocardiograms
papers.key_result: Proof-of-concept AI detection of severe AS phenotype on 530,871 echocardiograms (per title); abstract not available via PubMed, Crossref or Europe PMC on 2026-09-05, so metrics not recorded.

papers.title: Enhanced detection of severe aortic stenosis via artificial intelligence: a clinical cohort study
papers.key_result: 631,824 individuals / 1.08 million echos split 70:30; MDN model trained on 442,276 individuals to predict AVA<1 cm2; AUROC 0.986 (0.985-0.987); 4,622/88,199 (5.2%) high-probability severe AS of whom 77.2% met guideline severe AS; 5-year mortality 67.9% high vs 19.2% low probability (adjusted OR 2.41). The 631,824 / 442,276 figures match the FDA summary's development set, but the paper's independent evaluation cohort is 184,301 (30%) individuals versus 189,548 stated in the FDA summary (PubMed abstract, verified 2026-09-05).

papers.title: An Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Detection of Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Clinical Cohort Study
papers.key_result: AI-DSA applied to TTE reports of 31,141 US Medicare beneficiaries (2003-2017): sensitivity 82.2%, specificity 98.1%, c-statistic 0.986 for AVA<1 cm2 phenotype; identified an additional 1,034 (3.3%) with guideline-moderate AS but severe-AS phenotype (5-year mortality 73.5% vs 75.9% known severe, 44.6% without).

papers.title: Detection of severe aortic stenosis by clinicians versus artificial intelligence: A retrospective clinical cohort study
papers.key_result: Two tertiary centres, 9,189 adults with native valves: clinicians diagnosed 218 severe AS (2.4%); AI alert increased this to 376 (4.1%); women more often under-diagnosed (54.4% vs 38.6%, aOR 0.21).

papers.title: The National Echocardiography Database Australia (NEDA): Rationale and methodology
papers.key_result: NEDA registry methodology paper by the EchoSolv development group (435,133 individuals at time of writing); abstract states the data will inform analyses including 'the role of artificial intelligence to facilitate accurate diagnoses'. A direct statement that NEDA is the EchoSolv AS training source was not confirmed from abstracts in this session.

open_questions: Number and location of sites contributing the 6,268-study standalone cohort is not stated in the FDA summary (race categories suggest US data).
MRMC AUROC improvement (0.018) did not reach statistical significance (p=0.064) and the reported 95% CI is written as '0.037-0.001'; the summary nonetheless states improvement in all endpoints.
The summary reports 6,268 studies included but then '6,262 studies' when giving AVA distribution; discrepancy unexplained.
Training set size in TTEs (vs individuals) is not stated; 442,276 individuals is the training partition.

No clinicaltrials.gov registrations for EchoSolv were found in this session; company press mentions a 'flagship clinical trial' (72% more severe AS identified) without an identifier or peer-reviewed reference located here.
Playford 2020 abstract not retrievable via E-utilities/Crossref in this session; performance figures from that paper were not recorded.
Overall standalone AUROC 95% CI is given as 0.943-0.952 in the text (p.8) but 0.942-0.952 in the inputs table (p.9).

families.company: GE HealthCare (GE Medical Systems Ultrasound & Primary Care Diagnostics, LLC)
families.summary: AutoAS is a Breakthrough-designated AI software (product code POK, 21 CFR 892.2060) that analyzes B-mode PLAX, PSAX-AV and AP5 clips from compatible GE HealthCare ultrasound systems and returns 'suggestive' or 'not suggestive' of moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis with a study-level confidence score, intended as a point-of-care aid for deciding whether a full Doppler echocardiogram is needed. Cleared 2026-03-27 (K254161) with Ultromics EchoGo Pro (K201555) as predicate; standalone AUC 93.2% on 401 patients from four US institutions and a 5-reader, 220-case MRMC study showing +5.5% reader sensitivity.
families.intended_use_quote: AutoAS is a software application intended to assist medical professionals in the assessment of moderate/severe aortic stenosis (AS). The software uses an artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm to process previously acquired two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (2D-TTE) images to provide a suggestion of moderate/severe aortic stenosis along with an associated confidence metric that can be a diagnostic aid to a physician in a point of care or similar setting in determining if further evaluation is needed, including whether a full echocardiogram (2D, Doppler) needs to be performed. The results of AutoAS are not intended to be used on a stand-alone basis for clinical decision making and are not intended to supplement or replace a full echocardiographic examination. AutoAS results, along with the obtained ultrasound images, must be reviewed by a qualified physician. The AutoAS product is not intended to be used on patients who have prosthetic valves and/or have had prior valve repair or replacement. AutoAS software is indicated for use in adult patients and is intended to be an accessory to compatible ultrasound systems in environments where healthcare is provided.

notes: Three families, one clearance each, all product code POK under 21 CFR 892.2060 with Ultromics EchoGo Pro (K201555) as primary predicate. Verified 2026-09-05 against the FDA summary text (every quote located on the cited page), openFDA (decision dates, product codes, applicants all match), Crossref and PubMed (all 9 DOIs/PMIDs resolve with matching titles), ClinicalTrials.gov API (NCT05455541, NCT05631977, NCT06717373), and the company/press pages that were reachable (aisap.ai, dicardiology.com, echoiq.ai, withpower.com). Not reachable: aisap.ai/product (404), GlobeNewswire (connection failed), MobiHealthNews (403) - dependent claims marked unverified. AISAP and Echo IQ disclose training set sizes in their summaries (>140,000 exams at 2 institutions; 442,276 of 631,824 individuals); GE does not. Extra PubMed queries per family found no additional papers about the cleared products: Faierstein 2024 (JASE, Aisap.ai-affiliated echo age estimation) and Amster 2026 (EHJ-DH, Sheba POCUS biological age) concern features not in the cleared AISAP device; Playford 2025 (JACC Adv, Echo IQ AI-LVD) concerns LV dysfunction, not EchoSolv AS; nothing for AutoAS. Company-sourced figures that conflict with the FDA summary (AISAP six-site/24M-clip claims; Echo IQ '200M+ measurements' and '72% more' claims) are recorded as company/news, not as performance claims.
